head_commit.message:
PR #50225: [XLA:GPU] Support multi-output fusion in the concatenate emitter

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50225

📝 Summary of Changes
- The concatenate emitter emits fusions with several roots. Each distinct hero is computed once per operand loop, and one shared epilogue writes all outputs.
- UseConcatenateFusion accepts several roots when the heroes are concatenates with identical splits, the roots share one shape, and roots × operands ≤ 6. It rejects a non-elementwise op in the epilogue that reads a hero.
- The multi-output fusion pass merges concatenate fusions only if the result keeps the concatenate emitter.

🎯 Justification
Equal-shaped concatenates over the same inputs, as in the Eigh expander's Jacobi permutations, ran as separate kernels or fell back to the loop emitter. Now they run as one kernel that reads each operand once. This also merges RoPE q/k concatenate pairs in some models.

🚀 Kind of Contribution:  ⚡️ Performance Improvement,

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
This Eigh example gets a ~20% improvement on MI350:

```bash
HloModule Test
ENTRY Random_1000 {
  a.1 = f32[1000,1000]{1,0} parameter(0)
  ROOT CC = (f32[1000,1000]{1,0}, f32[1000]{0}) custom-call(a.1), custom_call_target="Eigh", backend_config="1,1,15,0.000010"
}
```

On gpt_j_6b, the RoPE q/k pairs merge in every transformer layer, but the overall end-to-end performance change is negligible.

🧪 Unit Tests:
hlo_fusion_analysis_test.cc and multi_output_fusion_test.cc cover the accepted shapes, the operand budget, mismatched splits and shapes, hero reads through non-elementwise ops (including inside the second sibling), and a layer-norm producer reduced from AlphaFold 3. Two FileCheck tests in emitters/tests/concatenate/ cover shape-changing epilogues and a shared hero.

🧪 Execution Tests:
Both FileCheck tests also run gpu_test_correctness on one GPU.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Defer CUDA VMM memory deallocations while a cuDNN handle is active.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Defer CUDA VMM memory deallocations while a cuDNN handle is active.

cuDNN v9 internally captures temporary CUDA graphs during heuristic queries and execution plan creation (e.g. via `cudnn::backend::cudnnBackendGetMetadataFromGraph` inside `cudnnBackendFinalize`), which does not go through `CudaStream::CaptureHandle`.

During parallel autotuning (`ConfigAssigner::GetConfigsForAll`), a worker thread running `GpuProfiler::Profile` can deallocate VMM buffers via `CudaDeviceMemoryAllocation::~CudaDeviceMemoryAllocation` -> `DrainPendingVmmDeallocations` -> `cuCtxSynchronize()` concurrently with the main thread querying cuDNN heuristics in `CudnnSupport::GetConvolveRunners`. Calling `cuCtxSynchronize()` while cuDNN is capturing a CUDA graph on the same CUDA context either fails with `CUDA_ERROR_STREAM_CAPTURE_UNSUPPORTED` / `cudaErrorStreamCaptureInvalidated` or segfaults inside `libcuda.so` (`cuCtxSynchronize`).

Call `CudaDeviceAllocator::EnterStreamCapture` and `CudaDeviceAllocator::ExitStreamCapture` in `CudnnHandle` (`xla/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_dnn.cc`) so that VMM deallocations are deferred until the active cuDNN operation completes.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1003451880

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Cache ContainsSignificantReduce and fast-path non-fusions in FusionInfoCache.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Cache ContainsSignificantReduce and fast-path non-fusions in FusionInfoCache.

In `PriorityFusionQueue::CanFuseWithNativeEmitter`, checking whether a producer or consumer contains a significant reduction (reduction factor >= 16) previously allocated an `HloFusionAdaptor` and traversed all instructions in the fusion on every `(producer, consumer)` pair without caching.

Move this check to `ContainsSignificantReduce` in `gpu_fusible` and cache the result for fusion instructions in `FusionInfoCache` (mirroring `ContainsScan`), guarding against zero-extent reduction output shapes before dividing. Also consolidate `FusionInfoCache` lookups into a shared `GetOrCompute` helper that evaluates non-fusion instructions (`instr.opcode() != HloOpcode::kFusion`) directly without acquiring `mutex_` or populating the cache maps, uses `absl::ReaderMutexLock` for concurrent fusion cache hits, acquires `mutex_` in `Invalidate`, and annotates cache maps with `ABSL_GUARDED_BY(mutex_)`.

head_commit.message:
PR #51246: [ROCm] Skip the hipGraphGetNodes count in PrepareFinalization on update

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51246

## 📝 Summary of Changes

`RocmCommandBuffer::PrepareFinalization()` returns early when the command buffer is being updated, so `Finalize()`
after `Update()` no longer asks HIP for the graph's node count.

## 🎯 Justification

Every time XLA updates a ROCm command buffer, it asks HIP how many nodes the graph has, and it does this right before launching the graph. HIP has no cheap way to answer: it topologically sorts the whole graph just to return the count. The count can't change during an update, so the work is wasted, and it sits on the host's critical path before every updated `hipGraphLaunch`.

Only `Create*` methods add nodes, and they all require `State::kCreate`, so the create-time finalization has already
made the graph non-empty.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

⚡️ Performance Improvement · 🧪 Tests

## 🧪 Unit Tests

`GpuCommandBufferTest.UpdateEmptyCommandBuffer` (`xla/stream_executor/gpu/gpu_command_buffer_test.cc`): an empty
command buffer is finalized, submitted, updated, finalized and submitted again. It covers the ROCm path and is skipped
on CUDA.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Defer CUDA VMM memory deallocations while a cuDNN handle is active.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Defer CUDA VMM memory deallocations while a cuDNN handle is active.

cuDNN v9 internally captures temporary CUDA graphs during heuristic queries and execution plan creation (e.g. via `cudnn::backend::cudnnBackendGetMetadataFromGraph` inside `cudnnBackendFinalize`), which does not go through `CudaStream::CaptureHandle`.

During parallel autotuning (`ConfigAssigner::GetConfigsForAll`), a worker thread running `GpuProfiler::Profile` can deallocate VMM buffers via `CudaDeviceMemoryAllocation::~CudaDeviceMemoryAllocation` -> `DrainPendingVmmDeallocations` -> `cuCtxSynchronize()` concurrently with the main thread querying cuDNN heuristics in `CudnnSupport::GetConvolveRunners`. Calling `cuCtxSynchronize()` while cuDNN is capturing a CUDA graph on the same CUDA context either fails with `CUDA_ERROR_STREAM_CAPTURE_UNSUPPORTED` / `cudaErrorStreamCaptureInvalidated` or segfaults inside `libcuda.so` (`cuCtxSynchronize`).

Call `CudaDeviceAllocator::EnterStreamCapture` and `CudaDeviceAllocator::ExitStreamCapture` in `CudnnHandle` (`xla/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_dnn.cc`) so that VMM deallocations are deferred until the active cuDNN operation completes.

head_commit.message:
Propagate buffer layout constraint across rank-changing bitcast-convert

When a bitcast-convert instruction adds or removes a trailing dimension and has
rank >= 2, layout assignment read the instruction's existing shape layout
instead of the incoming buffer layout constraint's minor_to_major order.
Instructions lowered from StableHLO do not yet have layouts assigned on their

debug builds that a layout was already present on the shape.

Propagating minor_to_major from the incoming buffer layout constraint without

cross-width bitcast-convert operations.

head_commit.message:
PR #51162: [ROCm] Hide GCC 8 std::filesystem symbols.

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51162

📝 Summary of Changes
`mori_application` no longer exports the GCC 8 `std::filesystem` code it links statically from `libstdc++fs.a` (`-Wl,--exclude-libs,libstdc++fs.a`), or its inline `path` members (`-fvisibility-inlines-hidden`).

🎯 Justification
The hermetic toolchain's GCC 8 `std::filesystem` is ABI-incompatible with the system `libstdc++.so.6`. MORI's exported copy took over hipBLASLt's calls. This affects ROCm tests that load MORI and call into hipBLASLt or other ROCm libraries that use `std::filesystem`.

display_title: [XLA] Speed up HloEvaluator::HandleReduce for integer, tuple, and large-output reductions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Speed up HloEvaluator::HandleReduce for integer, tuple, and large-output reductions.

Previously, `HloEvaluator::HandleReduce` used a fast path only for single-output floating-point scalar `kAdd` reductions. For integer reductions and variadic tuple reductions, `GenerateReduceOutputElement` ran an embedded `HloEvaluator` on every input element. Each reduction step allocated and destroyed scalar `Literal` objects and called `DecomposeTuple()`. In addition, for every output element, `GenerateReduceOutputElement` and `ShapeUtil::ForEachIndexNoStatus` allocated temporary index `std::vector` objects on the heap. On large reductions across many worker threads, these heap allocations caused high allocator lock contention and 900s test timeouts.

Extend `MatchSimpleBinaryReducer` to match single-output and variadic tuple reductions over simple scalar binary operations (`kAdd`, `kMultiply`, `kMaximum`, `kMinimum`, `kAnd`, `kOr`, `kXor`). Keep chunked `double` accumulation (`GetSumAsDouble`) for floating-point `kAdd` reductions. Evaluate all other matched binary reductions in native types over raw input buffers without heap allocations, and skip creating per-thread `embedded_evaluators`. Precompute linear strides per input argument (`SimpleReducePlan`) to iterate over reduced dimensions without per-output-element heap allocations or multidimensional index conversions. For general reductions that use the embedded evaluator, allocate `arg_values`, `accumulators`, and `embedded_operands` once per output element, and read tuple outputs with `LiteralSlice` instead of `DecomposeTuple()`.

This reduces unsharded `reduce_test_h100` (all 304 tests) runtime from over 2,300s (timeout) to 95.3s:
- `ReduceTestHlo.VariadicLaneAndMajorReductionWithLeadingTrivialDim`: >900s (timeout) to 0.232s
- `ReduceTestHlo.SingleOutputLaneAndMajorReductionWithLeadingTrivialDim`: 120.3s to 0.600s
- `GeneralReduceTest` (150 tests): 1,183.2s to 42.9s

display_title: PR #48089: [XLA:GPU] Fix loop emitter insert point after emitting a loop mid-block

head_commit.message:
PR #48089: [XLA:GPU] Fix loop emitter insert point after emitting a loop mid-block

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/48089

## 📝 Summary of Changes

Fixes #47372.

A sort comparator that computes non-scalar intermediate values crashes GPU
compilation with `llvm_loop.cc:76] Check failed:
!preheader_bb_->hasTerminator()`. The GPU nested computation emitter
(`CodegenNestedComputation`) emits comparators as inline functions with the
builder positioned before a pre-created `ret void`. The first multi-element
op emits its loop through `ForLoop::Emit`'s split path, which moves the
`ret` into the new `loop_exit` block. `LoopEmitter::EmitLoop` (and
`ForLoop::Emit` itself) then reposition the builder at the end of
`loop_exit`, which is after the moved `ret`. The next loop-emitting op sees
an insert point at the end of a terminated block and trips the CHECK.

The fix repositions the builder at the exit block's first insertion point
instead of its end, in both `LoopEmitter::EmitLoop` and `ForLoop::Emit`.
For the common case (the loop was emitted at the end of an unterminated
block, so the exit block is a fresh empty block) this is identical to the
old behavior. For the mid-block split case it puts follow-up code where the
original insertion point was: before whatever the split moved into the exit
block. `ParallelLoopEmitter::EmitLoop` already handles its exit block this
way; the shared llvm_ir helpers never did.

## 🎯 Justification

The module in the issue is valid HLO (plain ops, runs fine on CPU and
interpreter); the GPU backend aborts the whole process while compiling it.
Any custom sort comparator with non-scalar intermediates that survive
simplification hits this, as does any nested call computation emitted
through `CallNestedComputation`. The crash reproduces without any XLA
flags.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

## 🧪 Unit Tests:

`SortTest.MultiElementComparator` in `xla/tests/sort_test.cc`: sorts
`f32[32]` with a comparator that is semantically `p0 < p1` but computed
through `f32[2]` intermediates (iota, two broadcasts, two adds, elementwise
compare, slice, reshape), compared against the interpreter reference with
zero tolerance. Without the fix the GPU test dies on the `llvm_loop.cc:76`
CHECK; with the fix it passes. `sort_test_cpu`, `sort_test_nvgpu_any`, all
`//xla/service/llvm_ir/...` and `//xla/service/cpu/tests/...` targets pass
with the change.

## 🧪 Execution Tests:

The issue's original StableHLO module and a reduced 19-line HLO module both
compile and run on one GPU (RTX 2070, sm_75) with the fix and abort at the
CHECK without it. The fixed binary's outputs match the interpreter
elementwise for order-consistent comparators.
Copybara import of the project:

--
2b030bf33c80fbf195afa04ddbe31f0a17eb24b1 by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Fix loop emitter insert point after emitting a loop mid-block

ForLoop::Emit supports emitting a loop in the middle of a basic block by
splitting it; splitBasicBlock moves the tail of the block, including its
terminator, into the new loop_exit block. But after emitting the loop,
ForLoop::Emit and LoopEmitter::EmitLoop repositioned the builder at the
end of loop_exit, i.e. after the moved terminator. The GPU nested
computation emitter hits exactly this: it emits sort comparators inline
with the builder parked before a pre-created ret. A comparator with two
or more non-scalar intermediate values then crashes on the
llvm_loop.cc:76 CHECK when the second loop is emitted at the end of the
already-terminated loop_exit block.

Reposition the builder at the exit block's first insertion point
instead, which is where the pre-split insertion point's continuation
belongs. For loops emitted at the end of an unterminated block the exit
block is empty and this is identical to the previous behavior.
ParallelLoopEmitter::EmitLoop already handles its exit block this way.

Fixes #47372.

Merging this change closes #48089

head_commit.message:
PR #51324: Bump numpy from 2.4.6 to 2.5.4 Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51324 Bumps [numpy](https://github.com/numpy/numpy) from 2.4.6 to 2.5.4.
Release notes

Sourced from numpy's releases.

v2.5.4 (Oct 10, 2026)

NumPy 2.5.4 Release Notes

Released on 2026-10-10.

NumPy 2.5.4 is a patch release that fixes bugs discovered after the 2.5.3 release. Highlights are:

  • Many typing fixes and improvements,
  • A workaround for the MSVC 19.51 bug, see below.

This release supports Python versions 3.12-3.15.

Improvements

  • numpy.linalg.svd and numpy.linalg.lstsq now raise for inputs containing infinities instead of returning garbage results.

  • Fixed hangs in numpy.linalg.svd and numpy.linalg.lstsq for certain inputs containing infinities for recent versions of some LAPACK implementations.

  • numpy.linalg.cond now handles non-finite inputs more consistently.

(gh-32593)

StringDType hashing with NaN sentinels

StringDType instances with equivalent floating-point NaN sentinels now have equal hashes. Previously, distinct NaN objects could produce equal dtype instances with different hashes, causing dictionary lookups and set deduplication to fail.

(gh-32563)

Changes

MaskedArray resets a fill_value that cannot be represented in a new dtype

A fill_value copied from a source array is now reset to the default fill_value for the new dtype when it cannot be represented in that dtype. Previously the copied value could be stale: ufuncs that change dtype left the result holding a fill_value typed for the old dtype, which raised a TypeError only when something later validated it (such as .view()), and a floating point fill_value that overflows an integer dtype was kept as an out-of-range value together with a RuntimeWarning. Both now fall back to the default, including when a masked array is passed to MaskedArray with a different dtype. A fill_value given explicitly by the user is still validated and raises as before. This can now raise a ComplexWarning if the fill_value is complex and the new dtype is real.

head_commit.message:

  - Preload the kernel during Init and not afterwards. Otherwise *dread*locks.
  - Use nice things like command buffer nodes for ra2a instead of tracing.
  - When we use symmetric kernels shift ra2a to DebugOptions::COLLECTIVES_KERNEL so its enabled by default.

display_title: [Mosaic TPU] Prove divisibility through masks.

head_commit.message:
[Mosaic TPU] Prove divisibility through masks.

Kernels often round sizes and offsets to tiles with a mask, e.g. `(n + 127) & -128`. `isDivisible` could not see through `arith.andi`, so such values needed an explicit `tpu.assume_multiple` before they could slice a tiled dimension.

`isStructurallyDivisible` now proves `x & y` divisible by `2^k` if either operand is, since a mask keeps the low zero bits of both operands. The rule:

* applies only to power-of-two divisors, which covers tile sizes;
* only ever returns `true` or `nullopt`, because `x & y` can be divisible when neither operand is (`5 & 6 == 4`).

So it can prove more values aligned but never rejects anything that verified before.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1003817809

head_commit.message:
PR #51324: Bump numpy from 2.4.6 to 2.5.4 Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51324 Bumps [numpy](https://github.com/numpy/numpy) from 2.4.6 to 2.5.4.
Release notes

Sourced from numpy's releases.

v2.5.4 (Oct 10, 2026)

NumPy 2.5.4 Release Notes

Released on 2026-10-10.

NumPy 2.5.4 is a patch release that fixes bugs discovered after the 2.5.3 release. Highlights are:

  • Many typing fixes and improvements,
  • A workaround for the MSVC 19.51 bug, see below.

This release supports Python versions 3.12-3.15.

Improvements

  • numpy.linalg.svd and numpy.linalg.lstsq now raise for inputs containing infinities instead of returning garbage results.

  • Fixed hangs in numpy.linalg.svd and numpy.linalg.lstsq for certain inputs containing infinities for recent versions of some LAPACK implementations.

  • numpy.linalg.cond now handles non-finite inputs more consistently.

(gh-32593)

StringDType hashing with NaN sentinels

StringDType instances with equivalent floating-point NaN sentinels now have equal hashes. Previously, distinct NaN objects could produce equal dtype instances with different hashes, causing dictionary lookups and set deduplication to fail.

(gh-32563)

Changes

MaskedArray resets a fill_value that cannot be represented in a new dtype

A fill_value copied from a source array is now reset to the default fill_value for the new dtype when it cannot be represented in that dtype. Previously the copied value could be stale: ufuncs that change dtype left the result holding a fill_value typed for the old dtype, which raised a TypeError only when something later validated it (such as .view()), and a floating point fill_value that overflows an integer dtype was kept as an out-of-range value together with a RuntimeWarning. Both now fall back to the default, including when a masked array is passed to MaskedArray with a different dtype. A fill_value given explicitly by the user is still validated and raises as before. This can now raise a ComplexWarning if the fill_value is complex and the new dtype is real.

v4.38.3

  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.21.2 and earlier were discontinued on 24 September 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4188

CodeQL Action Changelog

See the releases page for the relevant changes to the CodeQL CLI and language packs.

[UNRELEASED]

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.3. #4256

4.39.0 - 15 Oct 2026

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. display_title: PR #51324: Bump numpy from 2.4.6 to 2.5.4

head_commit.message:
PR #51324: Bump numpy from 2.4.6 to 2.5.4 Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51324 Bumps [numpy](https://github.com/numpy/numpy) from 2.4.6 to 2.5.4.
Release notes

Sourced from numpy's releases.

v2.5.4 (Oct 10, 2026)

NumPy 2.5.4 Release Notes

Released on 2026-10-10.

NumPy 2.5.4 is a patch release that fixes bugs discovered after the 2.5.3 release. Highlights are:

  • Many typing fixes and improvements,
  • A workaround for the MSVC 19.51 bug, see below.

This release supports Python versions 3.12-3.15.

Improvements

  • numpy.linalg.svd and numpy.linalg.lstsq now raise for inputs containing infinities instead of returning garbage results.

  • Fixed hangs in numpy.linalg.svd and numpy.linalg.lstsq for certain inputs containing infinities for recent versions of some LAPACK implementations.

  • numpy.linalg.cond now handles non-finite inputs more consistently.

(gh-32593)

StringDType hashing with NaN sentinels

StringDType instances with equivalent floating-point NaN sentinels now have equal hashes. Previously, distinct NaN objects could produce equal dtype instances with different hashes, causing dictionary lookups and set deduplication to fail.

(gh-32563)

Changes

MaskedArray resets a fill_value that cannot be represented in a new dtype

A fill_value copied from a source array is now reset to the default fill_value for the new dtype when it cannot be represented in that dtype. Previously the copied value could be stale: ufuncs that change dtype left the result holding a fill_value typed for the old dtype, which raised a TypeError only when something later validated it (such as .view()), and a floating point fill_value that overflows an integer dtype was kept as an out-of-range value together with a RuntimeWarning. Both now fall back to the default, including when a masked array is passed to MaskedArray with a different dtype. A fill_value given explicitly by the user is still validated and raises as before. This can now raise a ComplexWarning if the fill_value is complex and the new dtype is real.

v2.5.0

This release moves the action to Scorecard v5.6.0, the first Scorecard release since its hosted services moved to new infrastructure.

For changes to checks and results, and what the infrastructure move means for you, see the Scorecard v5.6.0 release notes.

  • The action no longer prints the GitHub token variable while validating its options. by @​arpitjain099 in ossf/scorecard-action#1709
  • results_format accepts intoto, which wraps the JSON results in an in-toto attestation statement. by @​puerco in ossf/scorecard-action#1702

Other

  • Bump Scorecard to the v5.6.0 candidate and fix the canary toolchain by @​justaugustus in ossf/scorecard-action#1714

New Contributors

Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/upload-sarif's releases.

v4.38.3

  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.21.2 and earlier were discontinued on 24 September 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4188
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.2. #4203
  • Fixed a bug where the decision of whether to use a per-language bundle did not account for custom configurations that reference queries outside of compiled CodeQL packs. This issue was caught during internal testing and did not affect any customer repositories. We will resume the roll out of per-language bundles in the coming weeks. #4184

v4.38.2

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.1. #4160
Changelog

Sourced from github/codeql-action/upload-sarif's changelog.

CodeQL Action Changelog

See the releases page for the relevant changes to the CodeQL CLI and language packs.

[UNRELEASED]

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.3. #4256

4.39.0 - 15 Oct 2026

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198

4.38.3 - 08 Oct 2026

  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.21.2 and earlier were discontinued on 24 September 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4188
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.2. #4203
  • Fixed a bug where the decision of whether to use a per-language bundle did not account for custom configurations that reference queries outside of compiled CodeQL packs. This issue was caught during internal testing and did not affect any customer repositories. We will resume the roll out of per-language bundles in the coming weeks. #4184

4.38.2 - 24 Sept 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.1. #4160

4.38.1 - 18 Sept 2026

  • The CodeQL Action now has experimental support for CodeQL releases for which per-language bundles are available. Per-language bundles support analysis for a single language and are therefore smaller than the combined bundles that allow analysis for all supported languages. As a result, per-language bundles take up less space on disk and are faster to download. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in the coming weeks. #4146

4.38.0 - 09 Sept 2026

  • On GitHub-hosted runners, the CodeQL Action now deletes unused CodeQL bundles from the toolcache before downloading a different bundle, which frees up disk space for the analysis. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in September. #4124
  • The CodeQL Action now supports CodeQL releases that are compatible with Linux Arm64 and downloads the native linux-arm64 CodeQL bundle when available. #4072
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.0. #4129

4.37.9 - 26 Aug 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.4. #4106

4.37.8 - 21 Aug 2026

No user facing changes.

4.37.7 - 13 Aug 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.3. #4085

4.37.6 - 04 Aug 2026

  • Changed the default filepath for the new remote file address format that was introduced in CodeQL Action 4.37.0 / 3.37.0 to .github/codeql-config.yml to align it with the suggested path that is used elsewhere. #4070

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Defer CUDA VMM memory deallocations while a cuDNN handle is active.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Defer CUDA VMM memory deallocations while a cuDNN handle is active.

cuDNN v9 internally captures temporary CUDA graphs during heuristic queries and execution plan creation (e.g. via `cudnn::backend::cudnnBackendGetMetadataFromGraph` inside `cudnnBackendFinalize`), which does not go through `CudaStream::CaptureHandle`.

During parallel autotuning (`ConfigAssigner::GetConfigsForAll`), a worker thread running `GpuProfiler::Profile` can deallocate VMM buffers via `CudaDeviceMemoryAllocation::~CudaDeviceMemoryAllocation` -> `DrainPendingVmmDeallocations` -> `cuCtxSynchronize()` concurrently with the main thread querying cuDNN heuristics in `CudnnSupport::GetConvolveRunners`. Calling `cuCtxSynchronize()` while cuDNN is capturing a CUDA graph on the same CUDA context either fails with `CUDA_ERROR_STREAM_CAPTURE_UNSUPPORTED` / `cudaErrorStreamCaptureInvalidated` or segfaults inside `libcuda.so` (`cuCtxSynchronize`).

Call `CudaDeviceAllocator::EnterStreamCapture` and `CudaDeviceAllocator::ExitStreamCapture` in `CudnnHandle` (`xla/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_dnn.cc`) so that VMM deallocations are deferred until the active cuDNN operation completes.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1003451880

display_title: Deprecate `tsl::strings::LegacyPrecision` in favor of `absl::HighPrecision`.

head_commit.message:
Deprecate `tsl::strings::LegacyPrecision` in favor of `absl::HighPrecision`.

`LegacyPrecision(float)` and `LegacyPrecision(double)` now forward to
`absl::HighPrecision`, and the custom `FpToBuffer` implementation is removed.

This is a value-preserving but not byte-identical change in formatting:
- float: the old implementation used %.6g and fell back to %.9g. absl uses
  the shortest of 6-9 significant digits that round-trips, e.g.
  1.17549435e-38f is now printed as "1.1754944e-38". This matches what the
  header comment already documented (%.6g, %.7g, %.8g, or %.9g).
- double: unchanged (%.15g, falling back to %.17g).
- NaN with the sign bit set is now printed as "nan" instead of "-nan".

All outputs still round-trip to the exact same value.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1003771966

display_title: PR #51182: [CPU] Coalesce tuple all-reduce buffers for Gloo

head_commit.message:
PR #51182: [CPU] Coalesce tuple all-reduce buffers for Gloo

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51182

# [CPU] Coalesce tuple all-reduce buffers for Gloo

CPU tuple all-reduces currently invoke Gloo once per buffer, paying synchronous ring latency for each parameter even when the compiler combines the operation. This change reduces compatible buffers together.

Fixes #50283.

### Summary of Changes

- Add `Communicator::AllReduceMany` with a default per-buffer implementation and route the CPU all-reduce thunk through it.
- Override the batch operation in Gloo: group buffers deterministically by datatype, pack into aligned temporary storage, perform one reduction per nonempty group, and unpack successful results.
- Preserve the single-buffer direct path and existing behavior for other communicator backends.
- Validate buffer sizes and packed-size overflow, and keep scratch storage alive until the reduction completes.

### Justification

Combined gradient all-reduces with many small buffers pay repeated ring startup latency on CPU hosts. Coalescing buffers reduces collective calls from one per buffer to one per datatype group. Packing adds copies and two temporary buffers for the group being processed.

### Kind of Contribution

Bug Fix, Performance Improvement, Tests.

### Benchmark

End-to-end JAX timings and the public-HLO benchmark requested by this template have not been measured. No measured speedup is claimed. A regression test verifies the reduction in underlying collective calls.

### Unit Tests

Added tests for datatype grouping and collective-call counts, the default fallback, empty and single-buffer inputs, error propagation, oversized counts, and avoiding unpacking after a failed reduction.

### Execution Tests

Added a two-rank Gloo test covering mixed float/integer buffers, SUM/PRODUCT/MIN/MAX reductions, and separate versus in-place outputs.

Validation on Ubuntu/WSL with Clang 18 and Bazel 8.7.0 (`--config=clang_local -c fastbuild`):

- `//xla/backends/cpu/collectives:gloo_collectives_test`: all 186 tests passed, including the four new regression tests.
- `//xla/backends/cpu/runtime:all_reduce_thunk`: built successfully.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

display_title: Follow-up to review comments on cl/1003709391. The indexing cost model's estimates for scan fusions already decrease with the sequential tile size, so the near-tie tie-break towards larger sequential tiles is no longer needed: without it, the tiling search picks the same tiling for 126 of 128 benchmark scan fusions on H100 and B200, and the other two pick a sequential tile of 8192 instead of 16384 at estimates within 0.02%.

head_commit.message:
Follow-up to review comments on cl/1003709391. The indexing cost model's estimates for scan fusions already decrease with the sequential tile size, so the near-tie tie-break towards larger sequential tiles is no longer needed: without it, the tiling search picks the same tiling for 126 of 128 benchmark scan fusions on H100 and B200, and the other two pick a sequential tile of 8192 instead of 16384 at estimates within 0.02%.

Also rename a test whose name had double negations.

head_commit.message:
PR #50857: [XLA:GPU] Skip sibling fusion into small column reductions

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50857

📝 Summary of Changes

Skip a sibling multi-output fusion when one sibling is a column reduction whose grid has fewer blocks than the GPU has cores, and the other sibling is not a reduction.

🎯 Justification

Merging would run the non-reduction sibling on the reduction's small grid, which is slower than keeping them as two separate fusions.

🚀 Kind of Contribution:⚡️ Performance Improvement,

📊 Benchmark

detr -3%, and lit/lip/siglip/gemma3_4b ~-1% on MI300 and MI350

📝 Summary of Changes

Skip a sibling multi-output fusion when one sibling is a column reduction whose grid has fewer blocks than the GPU has cores, and the other sibling is not a reduction.

display_title: Deprecate `tsl::strings::LegacyPrecision` in favor of `absl::HighPrecision`.

head_commit.message:
Deprecate `tsl::strings::LegacyPrecision` in favor of `absl::HighPrecision`.

`LegacyPrecision(float)` and `LegacyPrecision(double)` now forward to
`absl::HighPrecision`, and the custom `FpToBuffer` implementation is removed.

This is a value-preserving but not byte-identical change in formatting:
- float: the old implementation used %.6g and fell back to %.9g. absl uses
  the shortest of 6-9 significant digits that round-trips, e.g.
  1.17549435e-38f is now printed as "1.1754944e-38". This matches what the
  header comment already documented (%.6g, %.7g, %.8g, or %.9g).
- double: unchanged (%.15g, falling back to %.17g).
- NaN with the sign bit set is now printed as "nan" instead of "-nan".

All outputs still round-trip to the exact same value.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1003771966

display_title: PR #51182: [CPU] Coalesce tuple all-reduce buffers for Gloo

head_commit.message:
PR #51182: [CPU] Coalesce tuple all-reduce buffers for Gloo

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51182

# [CPU] Coalesce tuple all-reduce buffers for Gloo

CPU tuple all-reduces currently invoke Gloo once per buffer, paying synchronous ring latency for each parameter even when the compiler combines the operation. This change reduces compatible buffers together.

Fixes #50283.

### Summary of Changes

- Add `Communicator::AllReduceMany` with a default per-buffer implementation and route the CPU all-reduce thunk through it.
- Override the batch operation in Gloo: group buffers deterministically by datatype, pack into aligned temporary storage, perform one reduction per nonempty group, and unpack successful results.
- Preserve the single-buffer direct path and existing behavior for other communicator backends.
- Validate buffer sizes and packed-size overflow, and keep scratch storage alive until the reduction completes.

### Justification

Combined gradient all-reduces with many small buffers pay repeated ring startup latency on CPU hosts. Coalescing buffers reduces collective calls from one per buffer to one per datatype group. Packing adds copies and two temporary buffers for the group being processed.

### Kind of Contribution

Bug Fix, Performance Improvement, Tests.

### Benchmark

End-to-end JAX timings and the public-HLO benchmark requested by this template have not been measured. No measured speedup is claimed. A regression test verifies the reduction in underlying collective calls.

### Unit Tests

Added tests for datatype grouping and collective-call counts, the default fallback, empty and single-buffer inputs, error propagation, oversized counts, and avoiding unpacking after a failed reduction.

### Execution Tests

Added a two-rank Gloo test covering mixed float/integer buffers, SUM/PRODUCT/MIN/MAX reductions, and separate versus in-place outputs.

Validation on Ubuntu/WSL with Clang 18 and Bazel 8.7.0 (`--config=clang_local -c fastbuild`):

- `//xla/backends/cpu/collectives:gloo_collectives_test`: all 186 tests passed, including the four new regression tests.
- `//xla/backends/cpu/runtime:all_reduce_thunk`: built successfully.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

head_commit.message:
Allow `PriorityFusion` to fuse producers into Triton scan fusions whose scans have a scan dimension of at most 128 (`kMaxRowLocalScanDimSize`). The row then fits into a single tile, so row-wise producers such as a softmax can be fused. For example, the softmax of a top-p sampling mask (softmax, cumsum, compare and select) can then be fused into the scan.

`FusionBlockLevelRewriter` re-tiles fusions whose sequential tile sizes no longer match their tiling space, e.g. after `HloCSE` merged reduces that producer fusion had duplicated.

With default flags, this change has no effect.

name: CI
display_title: Support `UnpinnedHostMemorySpace` in PJRT GPU.

head_commit.message:
Support `UnpinnedHostMemorySpace` in PJRT GPU.

PJRT GPU devices previously only attached device HBM and pinned host memory spaces, preventing callers from allocating, importing, or transferring buffers in `UnpinnedHostMemorySpace`.

Attach `UnpinnedHostMemorySpace` to each addressable GPU device and register `UnpinnedHostMemorySpace::kKindId` in `StreamExecutorGpuTopologyDescription`. In `PjRtStreamExecutorRawClient`, delegate buffer allocation, foreign memory import, and event creation for `UnpinnedHostMemorySpace` to `CpuRawBuffer` and `CpuEvent`, and enable zero-copy host buffer import on GPU for unpinned host memory. Update `PjRtStreamExecutorRawBuffer` copy paths to route transfers targeting `UnpinnedHostMemorySpace` through host memory copies rather than intra-client StreamExecutor device transfers.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1003742855

head_commit.message:
PR #50582: [ROCm] [CUDA] Serve MemorySpace::kHost from a host allocator in the VMM allocator PR 2/3

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50582

Note on these PR chains: PR3 looks large now but it has PR1 and PR2 changes as well. so, once those PRs go in PR3 rebase should bring it to shorter diff. also all three PRs touch shared XLA GPU code.
## 📝 Summary of Changes

`DeviceAddressVmmAllocator` takes an optional host allocator. When set, `MemorySpace::kHost` allocations come from it instead of device memory. They don't count against the VMM memory budget, are freed right away, and can be retried if a free fails. `AllowsAsynchronousDeallocation()` follows the host allocator, and `Map()` and the reservation-mapped `Allocate()` reject host memory.

Without a host allocator nothing changes. No caller passes one yet; PR 3 does.

Part 2 of 3:
1. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50581: VA remapping skips host memory space allocations. **Please merge it first**, since this PR makes the reservation-mapped `Allocate()` reject `kHost`.
2. This PR
3. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50583: the PJRT GPU client passes its pinned host allocators (the fix)

## 🎯 Justification

With the VMM allocator, `pinned_host` buffers get device memory, which the CPU can't access, so host reads and writes segfault (orbax checkpoint saves, for example). This lets the VMM allocator use real host memory for them.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

## 🧪 Unit Tests

`device_address_vmm_allocator_test`: host routing, map rejection, allocation and free failures, deallocation with the wrong device or size, duplicate addresses, asynchronous deallocation, and calling the host allocator without the device lock.

Copybara import of the project:

display_title: PR #51182: [CPU] Coalesce tuple all-reduce buffers for Gloo

head_commit.message:
PR #51182: [CPU] Coalesce tuple all-reduce buffers for Gloo

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51182

# [CPU] Coalesce tuple all-reduce buffers for Gloo

CPU tuple all-reduces currently invoke Gloo once per buffer, paying synchronous ring latency for each parameter even when the compiler combines the operation. This change reduces compatible buffers together.

Fixes #50283.

### Summary of Changes

- Add `Communicator::AllReduceMany` with a default per-buffer implementation and route the CPU all-reduce thunk through it.
- Override the batch operation in Gloo: group buffers deterministically by datatype, pack into aligned temporary storage, perform one reduction per nonempty group, and unpack successful results.
- Preserve the single-buffer direct path and existing behavior for other communicator backends.
- Validate buffer sizes and packed-size overflow, and keep scratch storage alive until the reduction completes.

### Justification

Combined gradient all-reduces with many small buffers pay repeated ring startup latency on CPU hosts. Coalescing buffers reduces collective calls from one per buffer to one per datatype group. Packing adds copies and two temporary buffers for the group being processed.

### Kind of Contribution

Bug Fix, Performance Improvement, Tests.

### Benchmark

End-to-end JAX timings and the public-HLO benchmark requested by this template have not been measured. No measured speedup is claimed. A regression test verifies the reduction in underlying collective calls.

### Unit Tests

Added tests for datatype grouping and collective-call counts, the default fallback, empty and single-buffer inputs, error propagation, oversized counts, and avoiding unpacking after a failed reduction.

### Execution Tests

Added a two-rank Gloo test covering mixed float/integer buffers, SUM/PRODUCT/MIN/MAX reductions, and separate versus in-place outputs.

Validation on Ubuntu/WSL with Clang 18 and Bazel 8.7.0 (`--config=clang_local -c fastbuild`):

- `//xla/backends/cpu/collectives:gloo_collectives_test`: all 186 tests passed, including the four new regression tests.
- `//xla/backends/cpu/runtime:all_reduce_thunk`: built successfully.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Run CublasPadForGemms right before GemmRewriter, also in fission.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Run CublasPadForGemms right before GemmRewriter, also in fission.

GpuCompiler ran CublasPadForGemms before GemmRewriter, through the virtual
AddPaddingForGpublasGemms method. This had two problems:

- GemmFusion fuses most dots into Triton fusions before this point, so the
  pass skipped them. FissionBackend can later rewrite such a fusion to
  cuBLASLt, but its pipeline did not pad.
- DotAlgorithmRewriter runs after the pass and makes new BF16 dots from F32
  dots. The pass did not pad these dots.

This change makes CublasPadForGemms take only the compute capability. The pass
now applies all cuBLAS padding requirements itself. The pass now runs right after DotAlgorithmRewriter and right before the non-FP8 GemmRewriter, in AddGemmRewriterPasses and in the cuBLASLt fission pipeline. The change removes AddPaddingForGpublasGemms and its per-backend overrides.
(Deleted the code for ROCm as after https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/33854 there's no padding anyway)

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1003727640

display_title: PR #48089: [XLA:GPU] Fix loop emitter insert point after emitting a loop mid-block

head_commit.message:
PR #48089: [XLA:GPU] Fix loop emitter insert point after emitting a loop mid-block

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/48089

## 📝 Summary of Changes

Fixes #47372.

A sort comparator that computes non-scalar intermediate values crashes GPU
compilation with `llvm_loop.cc:76] Check failed:
!preheader_bb_->hasTerminator()`. The GPU nested computation emitter
(`CodegenNestedComputation`) emits comparators as inline functions with the
builder positioned before a pre-created `ret void`. The first multi-element
op emits its loop through `ForLoop::Emit`'s split path, which moves the
`ret` into the new `loop_exit` block. `LoopEmitter::EmitLoop` (and
`ForLoop::Emit` itself) then reposition the builder at the end of
`loop_exit`, which is after the moved `ret`. The next loop-emitting op sees
an insert point at the end of a terminated block and trips the CHECK.

The fix repositions the builder at the exit block's first insertion point
instead of its end, in both `LoopEmitter::EmitLoop` and `ForLoop::Emit`.
For the common case (the loop was emitted at the end of an unterminated
block, so the exit block is a fresh empty block) this is identical to the
old behavior. For the mid-block split case it puts follow-up code where the
original insertion point was: before whatever the split moved into the exit
block. `ParallelLoopEmitter::EmitLoop` already handles its exit block this
way; the shared llvm_ir helpers never did.

## 🎯 Justification

The module in the issue is valid HLO (plain ops, runs fine on CPU and
interpreter); the GPU backend aborts the whole process while compiling it.
Any custom sort comparator with non-scalar intermediates that survive
simplification hits this, as does any nested call computation emitted
through `CallNestedComputation`. The crash reproduces without any XLA
flags.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

## 🧪 Unit Tests:

`SortTest.MultiElementComparator` in `xla/tests/sort_test.cc`: sorts
`f32[32]` with a comparator that is semantically `p0 < p1` but computed
through `f32[2]` intermediates (iota, two broadcasts, two adds, elementwise
compare, slice, reshape), compared against the interpreter reference with
zero tolerance. Without the fix the GPU test dies on the `llvm_loop.cc:76`
CHECK; with the fix it passes. `sort_test_cpu`, `sort_test_nvgpu_any`, all
`//xla/service/llvm_ir/...` and `//xla/service/cpu/tests/...` targets pass
with the change.

## 🧪 Execution Tests:

The issue's original StableHLO module and a reduced 19-line HLO module both
compile and run on one GPU (RTX 2070, sm_75) with the fix and abort at the
CHECK without it. The fixed binary's outputs match the interpreter
elementwise for order-consistent comparators.
Copybara import of the project:

--
2b030bf33c80fbf195afa04ddbe31f0a17eb24b1 by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Fix loop emitter insert point after emitting a loop mid-block

ForLoop::Emit supports emitting a loop in the middle of a basic block by
splitting it; splitBasicBlock moves the tail of the block, including its
terminator, into the new loop_exit block. But after emitting the loop,
ForLoop::Emit and LoopEmitter::EmitLoop repositioned the builder at the
end of loop_exit, i.e. after the moved terminator. The GPU nested
computation emitter hits exactly this: it emits sort comparators inline
with the builder parked before a pre-created ret. A comparator with two
or more non-scalar intermediate values then crashes on the
llvm_loop.cc:76 CHECK when the second loop is emitted at the end of the
already-terminated loop_exit block.

Reposition the builder at the exit block's first insertion point
instead, which is where the pre-split insertion point's continuation
belongs. For loops emitted at the end of an unterminated block the exit
block is empty and this is identical to the previous behavior.
ParallelLoopEmitter::EmitLoop already handles its exit block this way.

Fixes #47372.

Merging this change closes #48089

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add producer fencing to SchedulerMemoryFencing

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add producer fencing to SchedulerMemoryFencing

Consumer-side fencing bounds how late the users of a large buffer may run,
but the latency-hiding scheduler can still hoist the producers of other
large buffers far ahead of their reference positions, which lengthens their
live ranges and raises peak memory. Add an optional producer-side fence:
with --xla_gpu_experimental_scheduler_memory_fencing_producer_slack_windows=N
(default -1, disabled) every producer of a fenced buffer gets a control
dependency from the async start N windows before the last window that begins
ahead of the producer in the pre-LHS schedule. All added edges point forward
in the reference schedule, so they cannot create cycles.

display_title: PR #50582: [ROCm] [CUDA] Serve MemorySpace::kHost from a host allocator in the VMM allocator PR 2/3

head_commit.message:
PR #50582: [ROCm] [CUDA] Serve MemorySpace::kHost from a host allocator in the VMM allocator PR 2/3

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50582

Note on these PR chains: PR3 looks large now but it has PR1 and PR2 changes as well. so, once those PRs go in PR3 rebase should bring it to shorter diff. also all three PRs touch shared XLA GPU code.
## 📝 Summary of Changes

`DeviceAddressVmmAllocator` takes an optional host allocator. When set, `MemorySpace::kHost` allocations come from it instead of device memory. They don't count against the VMM memory budget, are freed right away, and can be retried if a free fails. `AllowsAsynchronousDeallocation()` follows the host allocator, and `Map()` and the reservation-mapped `Allocate()` reject host memory.

Without a host allocator nothing changes. No caller passes one yet; PR 3 does.

Part 2 of 3:
1. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50581: VA remapping skips host memory space allocations. **Please merge it first**, since this PR makes the reservation-mapped `Allocate()` reject `kHost`.
2. This PR
3. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50583: the PJRT GPU client passes its pinned host allocators (the fix)

## 🎯 Justification

With the VMM allocator, `pinned_host` buffers get device memory, which the CPU can't access, so host reads and writes segfault (orbax checkpoint saves, for example). This lets the VMM allocator use real host memory for them.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

## 🧪 Unit Tests

`device_address_vmm_allocator_test`: host routing, map rejection, allocation and free failures, deallocation with the wrong device or size, duplicate addresses, asynchronous deallocation, and calling the host allocator without the device lock.

head_commit.message:
A tiled `kScan` now leaves its `scf.for` over the scan dimension open (`SetOpenScanLoop`), so that elementwise epilogues and the `xtile.insert` of the fusion roots are emitted inside the loop, where the current scan tile is live. `EmitGeneric` closes the loop after writing all roots and keeps the induction variable bound until then. Tiled scans are emitted first, so that epilogue instructions tiled along the scan dimension (e.g. an `iota`) can use the induction variable.

`PriorityFusion` now fuses epilogues into Triton scan fusions. Fusing producers into scan fusions and fusions with more than one tiled scan remain unsupported.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Run CublasPadForGemms right before GemmRewriter, also in fission.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Run CublasPadForGemms right before GemmRewriter, also in fission.

GpuCompiler ran CublasPadForGemms before GemmRewriter, through the virtual
AddPaddingForGpublasGemms method. This had two problems:

- GemmFusion fuses most dots into Triton fusions before this point, so the
  pass skipped them. FissionBackend can later rewrite such a fusion to
  cuBLASLt, but its pipeline did not pad.
- DotAlgorithmRewriter runs after the pass and makes new BF16 dots from F32
  dots. The pass did not pad these dots.

This change makes CublasPadForGemms take only the compute capability. The pass
now applies all cuBLAS padding requirements itself. The pass now runs right after DotAlgorithmRewriter and right before the non-FP8 GemmRewriter, in AddGemmRewriterPasses and in the cuBLASLt fission pipeline. The change removes AddPaddingForGpublasGemms and its per-backend overrides.
(Deleted the code for ROCm as after https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/33854 there's no padding anyway)

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1002254943

name: CI
display_title: Use the `sequential_tile_sizes` of `BlockLevelFusionConfig` for scan fusions: the tile size of the scan dimension goes there instead of into `output_tiles`.

head_commit.message:
Use the `sequential_tile_sizes` of `BlockLevelFusionConfig` for scan fusions: the tile size of the scan dimension goes there instead of into `output_tiles`.

In `TilingSpace`:

- Propagate dimensions through elementwise instructions across the producer-consumer fusion boundary (`ProcessElementwise`), so that a scan finds its dimension below an elementwise epilogue.
- Fail with `Unimplemented` if a scan dimension cannot be located, instead of tiling it as a parallel dimension. The experimental emitter also checks that an unlooped scan tile spans the whole scan dimension.

In `GpuIndexingPerformanceModel`:

- Count root tile executions instead of launched blocks when accumulating per-block traffic: each block of a tiled scan loops over the scan dimension and recomputes the root region `CeilOfRatio(scan_dim_size, tile_size)` times.
- Implement `FlopsPerElement` for `kScan` and `kGetTupleElement`. The latter used to fall back to `HloCostAnalysis::RevisitInstruction`, which races when `PriorityFusion` estimates fusions concurrently.
- For scan fusions, put the tile sizes of the sequential dimensions into `sequential_tile_sizes` instead of the output tile sizes.
- For scan fusions, break near-ties (within 1% of the best estimated execution time) towards larger sequential tile sizes.
- Estimate `__triton` fusions without a block-level config with the tiling that `FusionBlockLevelRewriter` would pick, instead of treating them as infinitely expensive.

In `FusionBlockLevelRewriter`, always tile `__triton` fusions without a block-level config, since the Triton emitter requires one. This lets passes such as `ScanRewriterTriton` leave the tiling to the rewriter.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1003709391

display_title: PR #51182: [CPU] Coalesce tuple all-reduce buffers for Gloo

head_commit.message:
PR #51182: [CPU] Coalesce tuple all-reduce buffers for Gloo

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51182

# [CPU] Coalesce tuple all-reduce buffers for Gloo

CPU tuple all-reduces currently invoke Gloo once per buffer, paying synchronous ring latency for each parameter even when the compiler combines the operation. This change reduces compatible buffers together.

Fixes #50283.

### Summary of Changes

- Add `Communicator::AllReduceMany` with a default per-buffer implementation and route the CPU all-reduce thunk through it.
- Override the batch operation in Gloo: group buffers deterministically by datatype, pack into aligned temporary storage, perform one reduction per nonempty group, and unpack successful results.
- Preserve the single-buffer direct path and existing behavior for other communicator backends.
- Validate buffer sizes and packed-size overflow, and keep scratch storage alive until the reduction completes.

### Justification

Combined gradient all-reduces with many small buffers pay repeated ring startup latency on CPU hosts. Coalescing buffers reduces collective calls from one per buffer to one per datatype group. Packing adds copies and two temporary buffers for the group being processed.

### Kind of Contribution

Bug Fix, Performance Improvement, Tests.

### Benchmark

End-to-end JAX timings and the public-HLO benchmark requested by this template have not been measured. No measured speedup is claimed. A regression test verifies the reduction in underlying collective calls.

### Unit Tests

Added tests for datatype grouping and collective-call counts, the default fallback, empty and single-buffer inputs, error propagation, oversized counts, and avoiding unpacking after a failed reduction.

### Execution Tests

Added a two-rank Gloo test covering mixed float/integer buffers, SUM/PRODUCT/MIN/MAX reductions, and separate versus in-place outputs.

Validation on Ubuntu/WSL with Clang 18 and Bazel 8.7.0 (`--config=clang_local -c fastbuild`):

- `//xla/backends/cpu/collectives:gloo_collectives_test`: all 186 tests passed, including the four new regression tests.
- `//xla/backends/cpu/runtime:all_reduce_thunk`: built successfully.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

head_commit.message:
PR #51219: Preserve explicit result layouts alongside AUTO tuple outputs

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51219

## 📝 Summary of Changes

Preserve explicitly requested result layouts when other tuple leaves use AUTO layout. `LayoutAssignment::AssignLayouts` previously skipped root-copy enforcement unless every leaf had a layout, allowing later propagation to overwrite explicit constraints. Fill only AUTO leaves from the assigned root, then apply the existing copy logic to enforce explicit layouts.

Add a nested-tuple regression with repeated operands and update the host-memory conflict test to require the requested output layout while preserving memory-space coverage.

## 🎯 Justification

Fixes a Gemma2-2B BF16 decode failure where XLA returned `major_to_minor=(1,0,2,3)` instead of the requested `(1,2,0,3)` for `bfloat16[1024,4,256,256]`. This preserves the output-layout contract for workloads that mix explicit and AUTO result layouts, without requiring a MaxText workaround.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

## 🧪 Unit Tests

- Added a regression covering nested tuples, repeated operands, and mixed explicit/AUTO result layouts; it fails before the fix, and all 91 layout-assignment tests pass with the fix.
- Testing used an earlier upstream base with identical changed files; the suite was not rerun after rebasing.

## 🧪 Execution Tests

- All 12 single-GPU BF16 reproducer cases pass with exact numerical equality, including six mixed-layout cases that failed before the fix; the reproducer is not registered as a CI test.
- Gemma2 BF16 prefill/decode validation passes with finite logits and no explicit output-layout mismatches, using an earlier runtime with the fix applied.

head_commit.message:
PR #50581: [ROCm] [CUDA] Do not VA-remap host memory space allocations in command buffers PR 1/3

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50581

Note on these PR chains: PR3 looks large now but it has PR1 and PR2 changes as well. so, once those PRs go in PR3 rebase should bring it to shorter diff. also all three PRs touch shared XLA GPU code. I have tested all three on CUDA and ROCm but I don't have access to OneAPI. if I have missed any code changes that has negative effect on oneAPI can any reviewer know ?

## 📝 Summary of Changes

This issue is in both CUDA and ROCm. I noticed this while running resnet benchmark.

Command buffer VA remapping (`SKIP_TEMP`, `SKIP_PROFILED`) now skips host memory space allocations. Command buffers keep updating their addresses, like any other allocation that isn't remapped.

Part 1 of 3 to make `pinned_host` buffers work with the VMM allocator:
1. This PR
2. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50582: the VMM allocator serves `MemorySpace::kHost` from a host allocator
3. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50583: the PJRT GPU client passes its pinned host allocators (the fix)

## 🎯 Justification

Remapping backs an allocation with VMM device memory, but host memory space allocations must stay in host memory. PR 2 and PR 3 make the VMM allocator serve them from host memory, which fixes segfaults on CPU access to `pinned_host` buffers. This PR goes first so remapping never touches them. I noticed this problem while running resenet benchmark and decided to take crack at it.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

## 🧪 Unit Tests

`gpu_executable_va_remap_allocator_test`: a host memory space temp is not remapped under `SKIP_TEMP`, and a stable host memory space output is never selected under `SKIP_PROFILED`. A device temp is the control. With a device temp and a host memory space temp in the same command buffer, remapping stays active: the device temp is remapped into the VA reservation and is persistent, while the host temp keeps its own address and is not persistent.

Command buffer VA remapping (SKIP_TEMP, SKIP_PROFILED) now skips host

updating their addresses like any other allocation that isn't remapped.

This prepares for the VMM allocator serving the host memory space from

PR #50857: [XLA:GPU] Skip sibling fusion into small column reductions

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50857

📝 Summary of Changes

Skip a sibling multi-output fusion when one sibling is a column reduction whose grid has fewer blocks than the GPU has cores, and the other sibling is not a reduction.

🎯 Justification

Merging would run the non-reduction sibling on the reduction's small grid, which is slower than keeping them as two separate fusions.

name: CI
display_title: Avoid pointless GitHub CI runs on Copybara merges

head_commit.message:
Avoid pointless GitHub CI runs on Copybara merges

When Copybara merges a change, its `beforePush` hook force-pushes the finalized commit (with the submitted `PiperOrigin-RevId`) to the `test_<OCL>` PR branch right before pushing to `main` and closing the PR. This `synchronize` event triggers a fresh round of `pull_request` CI runs whose results are never checked.

To cancel those runs as soon as the PR closes, this change triggers `pull_request` workflows on `closed` events (with a PR concurrency group) while skipping all jobs when `github.event.action == 'closed'`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1003695675

head_commit.message:
Callers of `TransposePlan::ExecuteChunk` that allocate per-chunk buffers currently need to scan `InputChunkSizeBytes(i)` or `OutputChunkSizeBytes(i)` across all chunks to find the largest chunk size, as `TransposePlan` does not guarantee that chunk 0 is the largest.

Precompute `MaxInputChunkSizeBytes()` and `MaxOutputChunkSizeBytes()` during `TransposePlan::ComputeChunkSizes()` and expose them on `TransposePlan`.

head_commit.message:

PR #50581: [ROCm] [CUDA] Do not VA-remap host memory space allocations in command buffers PR 1/3

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50581

Note on these PR chains: PR3 looks large now but it has PR1 and PR2 changes as well. so, once those PRs go in PR3 rebase should bring it to shorter diff. also all three PRs touch shared XLA GPU code. I have tested all three on CUDA and ROCm but I don't have access to OneAPI. if I have missed any code changes that has negative effect on oneAPI can any reviewer know ?

## 📝 Summary of Changes

This issue is in both CUDA and ROCm. I noticed this while running resnet benchmark.

Command buffer VA remapping (`SKIP_TEMP`, `SKIP_PROFILED`) now skips host memory space allocations. Command buffers keep updating their addresses, like any other allocation that isn't remapped.

Part 1 of 3 to make `pinned_host` buffers work with the VMM allocator:
1. This PR
2. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50582: the VMM allocator serves `MemorySpace::kHost` from a host allocator
3. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50583: the PJRT GPU client passes its pinned host allocators (the fix)

## 🎯 Justification

Remapping backs an allocation with VMM device memory, but host memory space allocations must stay in host memory. PR 2 and PR 3 make the VMM allocator serve them from host memory, which fixes segfaults on CPU access to `pinned_host` buffers. This PR goes first so remapping never touches them. I noticed this problem while running resenet benchmark and decided to take crack at it.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

## 🧪 Unit Tests

`gpu_executable_va_remap_allocator_test`: a host memory space temp is not remapped under `SKIP_TEMP`, and a stable host memory space output is never selected under `SKIP_PROFILED`. A device temp is the control. With a device temp and a host memory space temp in the same command buffer, remapping stays active: the device temp is remapped into the VA reservation and is persistent, while the host temp keeps its own address and is not persistent.

display_title: Use the `sequential_tile_sizes` of `BlockLevelFusionConfig` for scan fusions: the tile size of the scan dimension goes there instead of into `output_tiles`.

head_commit.message:
Use the `sequential_tile_sizes` of `BlockLevelFusionConfig` for scan fusions: the tile size of the scan dimension goes there instead of into `output_tiles`.

In `TilingSpace`:

- Propagate dimensions through elementwise instructions across the producer-consumer fusion boundary (`ProcessElementwise`), so that a scan finds its dimension below an elementwise epilogue.
- Fail with `Unimplemented` if a scan dimension cannot be located, instead of tiling it as a parallel dimension. The experimental emitter also checks that an unlooped scan tile spans the whole scan dimension.

In `GpuIndexingPerformanceModel`:

- Count root tile executions instead of launched blocks when accumulating per-block traffic: each block of a tiled scan loops over the scan dimension and recomputes the root region `CeilOfRatio(scan_dim_size, tile_size)` times.
- Implement `FlopsPerElement` for `kScan` and `kGetTupleElement`. The latter used to fall back to `HloCostAnalysis::RevisitInstruction`, which races when `PriorityFusion` estimates fusions concurrently.
- For scan fusions, put the tile sizes of the sequential dimensions into `sequential_tile_sizes` instead of the output tile sizes.
- For scan fusions, break near-ties (within 1% of the best estimated execution time) towards larger sequential tile sizes.
- Estimate `__triton` fusions without a block-level config with the tiling that `FusionBlockLevelRewriter` would pick, instead of treating them as infinitely expensive.

In `FusionBlockLevelRewriter`, always tile `__triton` fusions without a block-level config, since the Triton emitter requires one. This lets passes such as `ScanRewriterTriton` leave the tiling to the rewriter.

display_title: Avoid pointless GitHub CI runs on Copybara merges

head_commit.message:
Avoid pointless GitHub CI runs on Copybara merges

When Copybara merges a change, its `beforePush` hook force-pushes the finalized commit (with the submitted `PiperOrigin-RevId`) to the `test_<OCL>` PR branch right before pushing to `main` and closing the PR. This `synchronize` event triggers a fresh round of `pull_request` CI runs whose results are never checked.

To cancel those runs as soon as the PR closes, this change triggers `pull_request` workflows on `closed` events (with a PR concurrency group) while skipping all jobs when `github.event.action == 'closed'`.

display_title: PR #51216: Reclaim unused regions in growing PJRT GPU memory pools

head_commit.message:
PR #51216: Reclaim unused regions in growing PJRT GPU memory pools

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51216

## 📝 Summary of Changes

Enable BFC's existing whole-free-region reclamation for PJRT GPU pools when `preallocate=false`, honoring `TF_ENABLE_GPU_GARBAGE_COLLECTION` with a default of `true`. Preallocated pools keep their reservation behavior. Gate the allocator test dependency behind `if_google` because OSS `xla_cc_test` adds it automatically.

## 🎯 Justification

Growing pools can retain separate, wholly free backing regions that cannot satisfy a larger request. When the remaining growth allowance is too small, allocation fails even though reclaiming those regions would permit the request within the configured cap. This affected Gemma2-9B and Gemma3-4B training.

The fix enables the existing reclaim-and-retry path without moving live allocations or raising the cap. The environment override makes the opt-out advertised by BFC's reclamation warning effective for PJRT pools. It does not address true capacity exhaustion or fragmentation within regions containing live allocations.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix · 🧪 Tests

## 📊 Benchmark

No performance improvement claim; earlier workload validation checked successful execution and finite losses.

## 🧪 Unit Tests

- Eight GPU-independent cases cover reclamation with the setting unset/enabled/disabled, live-allocation and capacity preservation, preallocated-pool retention, and invalid settings; existing upstream sizing tests are preserved.
- The earlier revision passed 59 allocator tests and failed the reclamation regression without the fix. This rebased revision passes formatting, whitespace, and static dependency checks; compilation and tests were not rerun because compute resources were unavailable.

## 🧪 Execution Tests

- Earlier manual four-GPU Gemma2-9B and Gemma3-4B training runs each completed 101 steps with finite losses, with recomputation enabled and disabled; these were not rerun for this revision. No automated execution tests were added.
- Both modes used the same earlier runtime with the fix applied, without a separate pre-fix baseline; the Gemma2 enabled run exercised profiling but did not accept the recomputation rewrite.

display_title: Add PjRtBuffer::UpdateSlice and PjRtRawBuffer::ScheduleUpdateSlice.

head_commit.message:
Add PjRtBuffer::UpdateSlice and PjRtRawBuffer::ScheduleUpdateSlice.

Adds `PjRtBuffer::UpdateSlice` and `PjRtRawBuffer::ScheduleUpdateSlice` taking `const StridedGather&` to update a strided slice of a buffer in place on host memory spaces (`pinned_host` and `unpinned_host`).

head_commit.message:
[SDY][cleanup] Use modifyAllArgAttrs and modifyAllResultAttrs in sdy_round_trip and shard_map_export.

Deduplicates manual DictionaryAttr loops over function argument and result attributes, skips setAllArgAttrs and setAllResultAttrs when no attributes change, and resolves 4 TODO(b/510714593) comments.
